info.short_name: Adenovirus Lab Tests (NREVSS, National and HHS Region)
info.long_name: Weekly number of nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for adenovirus reported to NREVSS, national and by HHS region
info.short_description: Weekly count of adenovirus NAAT tests reported by NREVSS laboratories, nationally and by HHS region.
info.long_description: Weekly number of nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs, e.g. PCR) for adenovirus performed by laboratories participating in CDC's National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System, as reported by CDC and served by the CMU Delphi Epidata API. National (data_nation.csv.gz) and HHS-region (data_region.csv.gz, geography hhs_1 to hhs_10) levels. Weeks with no value are missing from the CDC source; in HHS regions these are almost all weeks in which CDC suppressed a positive count of 1-4, and the test count with it. No values are imputed. NREVSS is a voluntary network of more than 450 clinical, public health and commercial laboratories, so values reflect testing of people who sought care, not population prevalence. Data are provisional for up to two years and recent weeks are revised as reports arrive.

delphi_nrevss.organization: Carnegie Mellon University Delphi Research Group

delphi_nrevss.description: Weekly laboratory testing data from CDC's National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS), accessed through the CMU Delphi Epidata API (v5). NREVSS is a voluntary network of more than 450 clinical, public health and commercial laboratories that report nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for respiratory viruses. National data cover adenovirus, SARS-CoV-2, rhinovirus/enterovirus, seasonal human coronavirus, human metapneumovirus, parainfluenza virus and RSV from July 2019 (SARS-CoV-2 from January 2020): weekly tests, positive detections and percent positivity, for the nation and for each of the ten HHS regions. State data cover only RSV and SARS-CoV-2, from February 2024, as CDC-published moving averages (3-week centered averages of tests and percent positivity, 5-week trailing averages of positives) for states that meet CDC participation criteria. Influenza is not included (it is reported through FluView). Weeks end on Saturday (MMWR weeks). CDC suppresses weekly positive counts of 1-4 and the matching test counts; these are left missing. Data are provisional for up to two years; recent weeks are typically more than 90% complete after about two weeks. Values describe people who were tested, not population prevalence, and carry no demographic detail.
delphi_nrevss.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions. Delphi lists this source as a public-domain U.S. Government work (17 U.S.C. 105).
